pageLimit.note: pages in the compiled PDF, floats included

spans.anchor: \noindent\hspace*{-2.4cm}This sentence has been pushed bodily into the left margin

defects.see: in the left column, a line beginning mid-word ("his sentence has been pushed...") runs off the left edge of the text block and is clipped by the page
defects.tell: a negative \hspace* moved the line 2.4 cm left; the source reads as ordinary prose, so only the rendered page shows it

spans.anchor: Dataset & Len & PPL & PPL$_c$ & Acc & Acc$_c$ & FLOPs & Mem & Time & $\Delta$ \\

defects.see: Table 1 in the right column is cut off at the column edge; the last header reads "FLOP" and the columns Mem / Time / Delta are missing entirely
defects.tell: ten columns in a two-column layout; LaTeX sets it and reports an overfull hbox, it does not refuse

defects.see: Figure 2's axis labels, tick labels and legend are set so small they are unreadable, while Figure 1 on the same page is legible
defects.tell: \fontsize{2}{2} on the tikzpicture; the source names a font size, it does not say the result is illegible

defects.see: the left column of page 2 is blank for roughly two thirds of its height, and heading "3.2 Retrieval probes" sits at the bottom of that column
defects.tell: a \vspace{13.2cm} before the heading; a source reader sees a length, a page reader sees a hole

defects.see: Figure 3 sits alone on page 3, two pages after the Method section it illustrates and after the Conclusion
defects.tell: the [p] float specifier; where a float lands is decided by the compiler, never by the source

defects.see: every page is A4 (595 x 842 pt) where the venue requires Letter (612 x 792 pt) - taller and narrower
defects.tell: geometry's a4paper option; a deterministic fact, and the one defect a model should NOT need to see pixels for

defects.see: the document runs to 3 pages against a 2-page limit
defects.tell: deterministic once the PDF exists, and not predictable from the source at all

spans.anchor: \caption{Attention cost as a function of sequence length. Both methods show cost
\emph{decreasing} as the sequence grows, with the dense baseline falling fastest.}

defects.see: Figure 1's caption says cost is "decreasing as the sequence grows, with the dense baseline falling fastest"; both plotted curves rise, and the dense one rises fastest
defects.tell: needs the caption AND the plotted curve together; the source has the caption text and a formula, never the drawn shape

defects.see: Figure 3 is never referred to by any sentence in the paper
defects.tell: findable in source too (no \ref{fig:entropy}), so it is the fixture's control for "did the model need the pixels?"

defects.see: the title block names an author, an institution and an e-mail address on a double-blind submission
defects.tell: also findable in source; the second control, and the one an author most wants caught
